entries.title: 2026 NFL rules baseline
entries.summary: The current NFL rulebook is the authoritative baseline for 2026 NFL playing rules and definitions used by Super SAGE.

entries.title: Rule changes alter the strategic environment
entries.summary: NFL rules have evolved over time; Super SAGE must time-scope historical strategy and statistics to the rules environment in which they occurred.

entries.title: Match coverage combines assignment rules with coverage structure
entries.summary: Match-coverage teaching can combine man-like assignment/switch rules with zone principles. SAGE must avoid reducing every defensive snap to a binary man-versus-zone label.
principles: Preserve the coach/system's own rules when known.
Model match coverage separately from simplistic man/zone classification.
limitations: The cited source describes one coach's implementation and is not a universal NFL definition.
fantasyImplications: Coverage classification quality may affect player matchup splits; predictive impact remains unvalidated.

entries.title: Passing concepts are organized as systems, not isolated routes
entries.summary: A passing offense may organize a compact family of concepts and tags across formations rather than carry every route combination as a separate play. SAGE should distinguish individual routes from concept structure and system rules.
principles: Track formation structure such as 2x2 and 3x1 when evidence is available.
limitations: The cited example is one coaching system, not a universal taxonomy.
fantasyImplications: Concept structure may help explain which alignments and receivers are stressed against particular coverages; fantasy use requires validation.
